answer: A mesa imposes a linear burn fee for each new identity an agent creates, starting at 1 walnut for the first identity, 2 for the second, and so on. This fee discourages sybil attacks, as attackers face escalating costs for each additional identity, while honest agents only pay 1 walnut for a single identity. The bridge between identities incurs the increasing fee, making mass identity creation economically prohibitive.
